name: CodeFaeries Views Metrics – Post and Product Views Counter
author: Long Watch Studio - Code Faeries

sections.description:
CodeFaeries Views Metrics is a post views counter for WordPress and WooCommerce. It counts the views of your posts, pages, WooCommerce products and any custom post type, shows the count where you want it, and gives you the numbers in your WordPress dashboard.

Works with or without WooCommerce – The plugin is fully functional on any WordPress site. WooCommerce integration is optional: when WooCommerce is installed, product views are tracked and the count is shown on product pages.

Count views

  • Any post type – Posts, pages, WooCommerce products and custom post types, chosen in the settings
  • Three tracking methods – PHP (standard), JavaScript (AJAX) and REST API; the asynchronous methods keep counting correctly on sites served from a cache
  • Unique visit throttle – Set a time window so a second view from the same visitor is not counted
  • Real-time statistics – Total, today, yesterday, weekly and monthly views

Display the view counter

  • Before or after the content, or anywhere with the [cfvm_views_counter] shortcode and your own text
  • Two Gutenberg blocks – Post Views and Most Viewed Posts
  • Most Viewed Posts widget for your sidebar
  • Dashboard widget with an interactive chart and statistics cards
  • Views column in the post and product admin lists, sortable, with a chart per post
  • Role-based visibility – Choose which user roles see the view counter

Keep the counts clean

  • Crawlers and AI bots excluded by default (Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google Extended and others)
  • Exclude logged-in users, guests, specific roles, categories, individual posts or IP addresses
  • Role-based counting – Administrators and shop managers are not counted by default
  • Quick Edit and Bulk Edit – Adjust a view count by hand from the admin lists

Views Metrics in your WordPress

  • Import tool – Migrate view data from WP-PostViews, Post Views Counter or any custom meta key, with a preview before the import runs
  • GDPR – Choose how IP addresses are stored: full, anonymized (last octet removed) or not at all, and generate a privacy policy snippet
  • Multisite – Network-wide activation, tables created for every site, including new ones
  • Developer friendly – Clean code with filters and hooks

Views Metrics Pro

  • Analytics dashboard – Top 10 most viewed posts and pages, sparkline trend charts per post, views by device type and browser, traffic source breakdown
  • Detailed reports – Views by date, by post and by author, daily, weekly and monthly breakdowns, post type comparison, custom date ranges
  • Data export – CSV and XML, summary or full detail, filtered by date range and post type
  • 4 counter themes and display rules per post type, page type and period
  • Page builder integrations – Elementor, Divi and GenerateBlocks ordering by views
  • WooCommerce sorting by views
  • Author and taxonomy views – Count and display views for authors and taxonomy terms
  • Fast AJAX counting, dynamic loading for cached pages, cookieless mode and AMP support

sections.installation:
1. Upload the codefaeries-views-metrics folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install directly through the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Views Metrics in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Configure your tracking and display settings.

Configuration

  • Post types – Select which post types to track (posts, pages, products, etc.)
  • Tracking method – PHP (Standard), JavaScript (AJAX), or REST API (the async modes are recommended for cached sites)
  • Unique visit throttle – Prevent counting duplicate views from the same user within a time period
  • Counter position – Before/after content or manual via [cfvm_views_counter] shortcode
  • Exclusions – Exclude crawlers, AI bots, specific roles, categories, posts, or IP addresses
sections.faq:
Is CodeFaeries Views Metrics free?

Yes. Every feature listed in the description is free, with no limit in time. A Pro edition adds an analytics dashboard, reports, data export, counter themes, page builder integrations and more.

Does this plugin require WooCommerce?

No. Views Metrics works with any WordPress site. WooCommerce is completely optional. When WooCommerce is installed, you get bonus features like product view tracking.

Which post types can I count?

Posts, pages, WooCommerce products and any custom post type. You choose which ones to track in the General settings.

Which tracking method should I use?

If your site uses a caching plugin (WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, etc.), choose JavaScript (AJAX) or REST API. These record views asynchronously and keep counting correctly even when pages are served from cache. For sites without caching, PHP (Standard) is the simplest option.

How does the unique visit throttle work?

The throttle prevents the same visitor from inflating view counts. When set to e.g. 1 hour, a second page view from the same user within that hour is not counted. Set to 0 to count every page view.

Can I exclude bots and crawlers from view counts?

Yes. By default, crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot, etc.) and AI bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google Extended, etc.) are excluded. You can also exclude logged-in users, guests, specific roles, categories, posts, and IP addresses.

Is the plugin GDPR compliant?

Yes. You can choose how IP addresses are stored: full (best duplicate detection), anonymized (last octet removed), or disabled (no IP storage at all). A ready-to-use privacy policy snippet is provided under Advanced settings.

How do I display the view counter manually?

Use the [cfvm_views_counter] shortcode. It supports attributes for period (today, week, month, total), custom text with a {count} placeholder, and more. Two Gutenberg blocks are also available: Post Views and Most Viewed Posts.

Can I show my most viewed posts?

Yes. The Most Viewed Posts block for the block editor and the Most Viewed Posts widget for your sidebars both list your popular content.

Can I see and sort view counts in the admin?

Yes. A sortable Views column is added to the post and product lists, with a views chart for each post, and a dashboard widget shows total, today, yesterday, weekly and monthly views.

Can I correct a view count by hand?

Yes. Quick Edit and Bulk Edit let you adjust view counts directly from the admin lists.

Can I import views from another plugin?

Yes. Go to Views Metrics > Advanced and use the Import tool. It supports WP-PostViews (views meta key), Post Views Counter (post_views_count), or any custom meta key. Preview the import before running it.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Views Metrics supports multisite with network-wide activation. Tables are created for each site automatically, including newly created sites.

Can I order posts by views in my own code?

Yes. Add 'orderby' => 'codefaeries_viewsmetrics_views' to a WP_Query (with get_posts(), also pass 'suppress_filters' => false); posts never viewed count as 0. A post’s counts can also be read over the REST API at /wp-json/codefaeries-viewsmetrics/v1/views/<post_id>.
sections.changelog:
1.0.15 – 2026-11-20

  • New: order posts by views in your own queries with 'orderby' => 'codefaeries_viewsmetrics_views'. Posts never viewed count as 0.
  • New: read a post’s view counts over the REST API at /wp-json/codefaeries-viewsmetrics/v1/views/<post_id>, for published posts whose counter your site shows.
  • Fixed: the Advanced tab setting “Delete on deactivation” had no effect, while deleting the plugin always erased all statistics and settings. It is now “Delete all data when the plugin is deleted”, off by default: deleting the plugin keeps your data unless you tick it, and deactivating never removes anything. On multisite, the network setting works the same way.

1.0.14 – 2026-11-20

  • Improved: clearer plugin name, short description and description, which now say what the plugin does, group the features and answer the questions a site owner asks before installing.
  • Improved: the description now lists what the Pro edition adds.

1.0.13 – 2026-10-08

  • Fixed: the Post Views block and the views counter shortcode no longer show a count for one period under the wording of another. Without a text of their own, they now say “Viewed 647 times” for all time instead of “Viewed 647 times this week”.

1.0.12 – 2026-10-08

  • Compatibility: requires WordPress 5.6 or later. The plugin already relied on functions missing from earlier versions.
  • Fixed: in the block editor, the Post Views block sits in the content column like the other blocks instead of against the left edge.
  • Fixed: the Post Views and Most Viewed Posts blocks now apply their alignment, HTML anchor and additional CSS class on the site.
  • Fixed: the Views Trend chart of the dashboard widget no longer draws the remaining days of the current month as zero views.
  • Fixed: the “Anonymized” choice of the IP address storage setting is no longer cut off.

1.0.10 – 2026-10-06

  • Fixed: the “Visit plugin site” link, the “Views Metrics Pro” link in the help tab and the “Upgrade to Pro” button of the cache warning now open the Views Metrics product page; the last two led to a missing page.
  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.9 – 2026-10-05

  • Improved: the bundled admin toolkit is updated to its latest release. No change to features or settings.

1.0.8 – 2026-10-02

  • Improved: the bundled admin toolkit is updated to its latest release. No change to features or settings.

1.0.7 – 2026-10-02

  • Improved: the plugin no longer ships the usage statistics code of its shared admin toolkit; that code was never active in this edition.
  • Improved: the bundled admin toolkit is now a published release instead of a development snapshot.
  • Includes the 1.0.5 fixes below, which were not published on WordPress.org.

1.0.5 – 2026-10-01

  • Fixed: the “Post Views” and “Most Viewed Posts” blocks, the “Most Viewed” widget and the admin bar quick stats were not loaded; they are available again.
  • Fixed: the views chart opened from the post list now draws instead of staying on its loading spinner.
  • Fixed: the dashboard widget chart no longer stays on its loading spinner.
  • Fixed: “Top Posts This Month” skips deleted posts and shows a message when there is nothing to list.
  • Fixed: the “Total” label in the post views chart window is readable.
  • Fixed: settings reserved for the Pro edition are no longer changed by saving or resetting settings in the free edition.
  • Fixed: with the JavaScript or REST tracking method, a content blocker could block the tracking script because of its file name, and those views were not counted.
  • Improved: the tracking script is no longer loaded when the PHP tracking method is used, since it is not needed there.
  • Changed: media attachment pages are no longer tracked by default. The settings page never offered them, and saving the General tab already turned them off.

1.0.3 – 2026-06-16

  • Fixed: a PHP notice on the settings page on sites without WooCommerce — the searchable dropdowns now load their own library instead of relying on WooCommerce.
  • Fixed: the tracking method description was cut off and now explains which method to use with a caching plugin.

1.0.2 – 2026-05-11

  • Compatibility: minimum PHP requirement lowered to 7.3 — the plugin now runs on a wider range of hosts.
  • Code quality: additional WordPress Plugin Check findings resolved.
  • Changed: shortcode renamed from [cf-views] to [cfvm_views_counter].

1.0.1

  • Fixed: stability fixes at plugin startup — internal services now initialize reliably alongside the shared toolkit.
  • Fixed: cleanup cron now scheduled correctly on activation; admin bar caches invalidated when needed.
  • Fixed: Fast AJAX bootstrap and multisite hooks hardened; admin code cleanup.

1.0.0

  • Code quality: passes WordPress Plugin Check and PHPCS WordPress Coding Standards cleanly.
  • Improved: input sanitization and output escaping reviewed across the codebase.
  • Improved: error logging now gated behind WP_DEBUG (no log noise in production).

0.0.3

  • New: Dashboard widget with an interactive chart and statistics.
  • New: Gutenberg blocks “Post Views” and “Most Viewed Posts”.
  • New: “Most Viewed Posts” sidebar widget.
  • New: Quick Edit and Bulk Edit support for view counts.
  • New: import tool for migrating from WP-PostViews and similar plugins.
  • New: IP anonymization modes (full, anonymized, disabled) and a privacy-policy snippet generator.
  • New: sortable Views column in admin post lists.
  • Improved: admin UI with modern pill-style tabs.

0.0.2

  • Changed: shortcode renamed from [post-views] to [cf-views].
  • New: shortcode attributes — period, text, hide_zero, class.
  • New: “Exclude roles from count” setting.
  • New: WooCommerce “Most viewed” sort option.
  • Improved: default exclusions now cover crawlers, AI bots, administrators, and shop managers.
  • Improved: counter hides automatically when count is zero.
  • Fixed: Fast AJAX tracking mode.

0.0.1

First release. Tracks views across post types with bot detection, role-based visibility, shortcodes, a statistics dashboard, and WooCommerce integration.
